name: Aeon-Tempest
specific_features: Storm eye that has remained geographically fixed for observed history
description: Aeon-Tempest is a gas giant defined by a single enormous storm eye that covers nearly an entire hemisphere. The eye has remained geographically fixed relative to the planet's rotation for as long as instruments have observed it, an atmospheric phenomenon that should be physically impossible given the planet's wind dynamics.

The toxic atmosphere is banded with methane ice clouds in shades of teal and deep indigo, circling the fixed storm eye in concentric rings. Sub-atmospheric lightning networks discharge continuously within the eye wall, creating a permanent ring of electrical fire around the calm center.

Atmospheric models consistently fail to predict the storm eye's stability. It should have dissipated or migrated within years of formation, yet it persists across what appears to be an aeon-scale timeframe. Some physicists have proposed that a massive structure beneath the cloud layer is anchoring the storm, though no probe has survived deep enough to confirm.

Helium-3 harvesting is conducted from the calmer bands far from the storm eye, where conditions are merely dangerous rather than lethal. The fixed storm remains one of the great unsolved mysteries of atmospheric science in this sector of space.
